title: LORM Policy
description: Machine-readable LORM policy document (SPEC.md §13). Conventionally stored as lorm-policy.yaml at the project root or .lorm/policy.yaml.

lorm_policy.description: Policy format version (independent of the LORM spec version).

owner.description: Person or team accountable for this policy document (the principal or delegate).

defaults.description: Behavior for action classes not matched by any capabilities[] entry.

max_level.description: Highest level any unlisted capability may operate at. RECOMMENDED: L3.

unknown_action.description: What a consumer does with an action class it cannot classify.

uncertainty_threshold.description: Diagnosis uncertainty above which a capability degrades one level and escalates (0 = no uncertainty tolerated, 1 = any tolerated).

log.description: Path (relative to the policy file) of the append-only audit log; JSON Lines.

record_fields.description: Fields every audit record must contain. MUST include at least the SPEC §10.3 minimum set.

demotions.description: Active demotions. A demotion entry OVERRIDES the listed level of the named capability (SPEC §6.5). Maintained by humans; the system may propose entries but never writes them (I-8).

until.description: Condition or date for re-promotion; re-promotion always follows the full SPEC §6.2 path.

id.description: Dotted action-class identifier (domain.object.verb). Consumers match exact first, then glob.

rollback.description: Concrete rollback procedure, or the literal string 'irreversible' (which SHOULD disqualify the capability from L5, SPEC I-7).

conditions.description: Preconditions that must hold before an L5 execution. Strings in this schema version: agent-interpretable, human-auditable. A structured machine-evaluable form is reserved for a future version.

match.description: Hard-enforcement matcher (schema 1.1+; MCP fields 1.2+). Consumed by the enforcement hook to deterministically map tool calls to this capability. Entries without match are enforced only by soft consumers (the agent skill). For command-shaped and MCP-shaped capabilities, command_patterns / input_patterns MUST encode the target scope (bounds.targets are only hook-verifiable for file paths).

tools.description: Claude Code built-in tools this capability can arrive through.

command_patterns.description: fnmatch patterns evaluated against each shell segment of a Bash command and against the raw command string.

path_patterns.description: fnmatch patterns against the project-relative path of a Write/Edit file_path. Note: '*' matches across '/'.

tool_patterns.description: Schema 1.2+: fnmatch patterns against the full MCP tool name (mcp__<server>__<tool>), e.g. 'mcp__postgres__query'. Avoid bare 'mcp__*' on L4/L5 entries — encode the server and tool.

input_patterns.description: Schema 1.2+: per-field fnmatch patterns against the MCP tool_input. Every listed field must exist and match (AND). Non-string values are matched against their JSON serialization. This is where the target scope of an MCP capability lives.

targets.description: Where the capability may act (paths, object names, environments); glob patterns allowed.

max_objects.description: Maximum objects a single action may touch.

max_actions_per_hour.description: Rate limit, evaluated against the audit log (SPEC 13-3).

expect.description: Declared expected outcome, checked after execution (SPEC §10.1).

window.description: How long after execution the outcome is checked (e.g. '30m', '24h').

policyBlock.description: L5 delegation metadata (SPEC §8). Required for every L5 capability.

approved_by.description: MUST differ from author (SPEC 8-1). Consumers SHOULD verify.

expires.description: Mandatory (SPEC 8-2). Expired => consumers treat the capability as L4.

tested.description: Evidence of testing before activation: what, when, outcome.
